Durchlauchtigster Fürst
Gnädigster Fürst und Herr!
Ich lag in heftigsten Fieber als Ewr Durchlaucht
Schreiben mir einging, die Ansicht Ihrer Hand
erheiterte meine Summe, aber wie groß war
mein Erſtaunen als ich das ausgestellte
Instrument nebst der Vollmacht Sache
wer hat Euer durchlaucht den den Rath gegeben?
W hier was für Ew Durchlaucht beyzutreiben,
so würde es ohne ein solches Instrument geschehen
Ich habe ja dazu General Vollmacht
Für Ihnen kan ich leider nichts beitreiben den
alles ist in diesen Augenblick mit arrest belegt
Überdies waren Sie ja schuldig die Zinsen an der
Invaliden Casse zu bezahlen.
Mich schleppte mann in Berlin Collé ich mußte
als mich die Franzosen in Arrest hielten, für Ewr
Durchlaucht als ihr bevollmächtigter bezahlen.
Als ich aus den Arrest entlaßen war bewies ich
das unerhöhrte ungerechte Verfahren des Intendanten
Maluce und der Invaliden Casse bey der Französischen
General Direction — diese nun befahl daß nur
die 3121 rt aus den Gütern nebst Kosten und
Zinsen zurück gegeben werden sollen.
Jemas dieses Decrets kan mir ich die Gelder
zu rück fordern, nicht Ewer durchlaucht, den
Sie sind der schuldige Theil — Ich fordere um
die Zinsen Intressen und Kosten welche zusammen
4219 rt. betragen, ich verlange daß selbige
mir aus den Reſten und Zinsen der Unterthanen
worauf jezt die Invaliden Casse Arrest gelegt
hat beigetrieben werden sollen.
Um nun dieſe Sache zu facilitiren und nicht erſt
weitläuftige richterliche Hülfe nachzusuchen
sollen nach dem Rathe des Komorniks, Ewr durch¬
laucht erklären.
daß Sie gemäs des Decrets des Französischen
General Gouvernements dem Krieges und
Forst Rath von Triebenfeld, die von ihm durch
zwang und Arrest abgenommene 3125 Rthl. pp. Zinsen
welche die Invaliden Casse 1808 d. 14t Febr gegen Quittung
in Empfang genommen, und welche das Französische
General Gouvernement dem p. v Triebenfeld aus
dem Zagorower Guts Revenuen zu Remtonschen
befohlen, noch schuldig wären und das der
p. v. Triebenfeld desfals wieder in Ansehung des
vorgeschoßenen Capitals noch der Kosten und
Intressen befriedigt sey.
Da nun das vorgeschoßene Capital nebst Zinsen
und Kosten 4219. rt. betrüge, so wiesen
sie dem Triebenfeld an diese Summa im betrage
von 4219 rt aus den Alten und neuen Zinsen
welche die Einwohner von Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica
Kopojno, Skokum, Swiątniki, Adelow, Sophienthal auf Alt und
Neu Swięce zu bezahlen habe, beziehen und sich aus diesen
fonds bezahlt machen könne.
Sie räumten zu dem Ende ein daß diese
mehr erwehnte Summa von 4219 rt sofort
durch einen Komornik und folglich durch der strengsten
Execution beygetrieben und bef dem von
Triebenfeld behändiget werden könne.
Dies läst den der Komornik vom Tribunal
Aproberen und sieht hernach zu was er vor
der Invaliden Casse weg darauf beitreiben
oder erwischen kan.
Es ist dies das einzige Rettungsmittel
etwas Geld jezt hier zu bekommen um
die Maschine im Gang zu erhalten
Ich sende daher nochmahls meinen Förster
zu Pferde und bitte Ewr Durchlaucht auf
das dringendeste das Instrument nach
vorbeschriebener Art auf das aller
schleunigste ausfertigen zu laßen und
es mir durch den Bothen zu übermachen
Ich ersterbe
Ewr Durchlaucht
wann ich das Instrument
nicht den 15 höchstens 16ten früh
hier habe so geht alles
zu Ende und fält über
haufen.
Blizanow
den 6ten July 1812
Unterthäniger dein
v Triebenfeld

Ewr Durchlaucht

mentions_english.display: the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld
mentions_english.surface_de: Krieges und Forst Rath von Triebenfeld
mentions_english.surface_en: the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld

translation.en:
18

Most Serene Prince

Most gracious Prince and Lord!

I lay in the most violent fever when Your Serene Highness's letter reached me; the sight of your hand cheered my sum, but how great was my astonishment when I [saw] the instrument that had been made out, together with the power of attorney — who has given Your Serene Highness this counsel? W here, what was to be collected in for Your Serene Highness, that would happen without any such instrument. I do, after all, hold a general power of attorney for that purpose. For you, unhappily, I can collect in nothing, for at this moment everything has been placed under arrest. Besides, you were indeed bound to pay the interest to the Invalids' Fund.

In Berlin I was dragged about Collé; when the French held me under arrest I had to pay, for Your Serene Highness, as your authorised representative. When I had been released from arrest I proved the unheard-of, unjust proceeding of the Intendant

Maluce and of the Invalids' Fund before the French General Direction — this body has now ordered that only the 3121 Rthl are to be returned out of the estates, together with costs and interest. [In accordance] with this decree it is I who can demand the monies back, not Your Serene Highness, for you are the party owing — I demand, over and above, the interest, the interest thereon and the costs, which together amount to 4219 Rthl; I require that the same be collected in for me out of the arrears and the interest of the subjects, upon which the Invalids' Fund has now laid arrest.

Now in order to facilitate this matter, and not first to have to seek out lengthy judicial assistance, Your Serene Highness should, on the counsel of the komornik, declare:

that you, in accordance with the decree of the French General Government, still owe to the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld the 3125 Rthl etc. of interest taken from him by compulsion and arrest, which the Invalids' Fund received against receipt on 14 February 1808,

names.de: Krieges und Forst Rath von Triebenfeld
names.en: the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld

translation.en:
and which the French General Government ordered to be [uncertain: reimbursed] to the said von Triebenfeld out of the revenues of the Zagórów estate, and that the said von Triebenfeld has in this respect been satisfied neither as regards the capital advanced nor as regards the costs and interest.

Since, then, the capital advanced together with interest and costs amounts to 4219 Rthl, you accordingly assign to Triebenfeld this sum, in the amount of 4219 Rthl, out of the old and new interest which the inhabitants of Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica, Kopojno, Skokum, Swiątniki, Adelow, Sophienthal upon Alt and Neu Swięcia have to pay, [so that he may] draw upon it and pay himself out of these funds.

To that end you concede that this above-mentioned sum of 4219 Rthl may at once be collected in by a komornik, and consequently by the strictest execution, and be handed over to von Triebenfeld. This the komornik then has the Tribunal

approve, and then sees what he can collect in or lay hold of upon it ahead of the Invalids' Fund.

This is the only means of rescue for getting any money here at present, so as to keep the machine going. text_english:
18

Most Serene Prince

Most gracious Prince and Lord!

I lay in the most violent fever when Your Serene Highness's letter reached me; the sight of your hand cheered my sum, but how great was my astonishment when I [saw] the instrument that had been made out, together with the power of attorney — who has given Your Serene Highness this counsel? W here, what was to be collected in for Your Serene Highness, that would happen without any such instrument. I do, after all, hold a general power of attorney for that purpose. For you, unhappily, I can collect in nothing, for at this moment everything has been placed under arrest. Besides, you were indeed bound to pay the interest to the Invalids' Fund.

In Berlin I was dragged about Collé; when the French held me under arrest I had to pay, for Your Serene Highness, as your authorised representative. When I had been released from arrest I proved the unheard-of, unjust proceeding of the Intendant

Maluce and of the Invalids' Fund before the French General Direction — this body has now ordered that only the 3121 Rthl are to be returned out of the estates, together with costs and interest. [In accordance] with this decree it is I who can demand the monies back, not Your Serene Highness, for you are the party owing — I demand, over and above, the interest, the interest thereon and the costs, which together amount to 4219 Rthl; I require that the same be collected in for me out of the arrears and the interest of the subjects, upon which the Invalids' Fund has now laid arrest.

Now in order to facilitate this matter, and not first to have to seek out lengthy judicial assistance, Your Serene Highness should, on the counsel of the komornik, declare:

that you, in accordance with the decree of the French General Government, still owe to the Councillor of War and Forests von Triebenfeld the 3125 Rthl etc. of interest taken from him by compulsion and arrest, which the Invalids' Fund received against receipt on 14 February 1808,

and which the French General Government ordered to be [uncertain: reimbursed] to the said von Triebenfeld out of the revenues of the Zagórów estate, and that the said von Triebenfeld has in this respect been satisfied neither as regards the capital advanced nor as regards the costs and interest.

Since, then, the capital advanced together with interest and costs amounts to 4219 Rthl, you accordingly assign to Triebenfeld this sum, in the amount of 4219 Rthl, out of the old and new interest which the inhabitants of Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica, Kopojno, Skokum, Swiątniki, Adelow, Sophienthal upon Alt and Neu Swięcia have to pay, [so that he may] draw upon it and pay himself out of these funds.

To that end you concede that this above-mentioned sum of 4219 Rthl may at once be collected in by a komornik, and consequently by the strictest execution, and be handed over to von Triebenfeld. This the komornik then has the Tribunal

approve, and then sees what he can collect in or lay hold of upon it ahead of the Invalids' Fund.

summary_en: v. Triebenfeld returns the instrument and power of attorney sent by the Prince, since he says he already holds a general power of attorney and everything has been seized. He says that under French seizure he had to pay the Invalids' Fund on the Prince's behalf. The French General Direction ordered the 3121 Rthl to be repaid out of the estates. He asks for a declaration assigning him 4219 Rthl from the arrears of interest owed by the inhabitants of Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica, Kopojno, Skokum, Swiątniki and other places, to be collected through a komornik.
summary_de: v. Triebenfeld weist das vom Fürsten übersandte Instrument samt Vollmacht zurück, da er Generalvollmacht besitze und alles mit Arrest belegt sei. Unter französischem Arrest habe er für den Fürsten an die Invaliden Casse zahlen müssen. Die französische General Direction ordnete die Rückzahlung der 3121 Rthl aus den Gütern an. Er verlangt eine Erklärung, die ihm 4219 Rthl aus den Zinsresten der Einwohner von Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica, Kopojno, Skokum, Swiątniki und anderen Orten anweist, beizutreiben durch einen Komornik.

reading.notes: Triebenfeld, ill with fever at Blizanow, writes to the Prince. He objects to the instrument and power of attorney the Prince sent, since he already holds a general power of attorney. The Invaliden Casse has put everything under arrest. While he was held by the French in Berlin he had to pay the Prince's debt, and the French General Direction ordered 3121 rt plus costs and interest repaid to him from the estates. He claims 4219 rt and dictates the declaration the Prince should issue, on the Komornik's advice: the sum is to be assigned to him from the interest arrears of the inhabitants of Wrąbczyn, Alt Olesnica, Kopojno and other places, collectable by execution. He sends his forester and needs the instrument by the 15th or 16th.
